title: Zinc oxide-containing material prepared in the presence of  Agrimonia eupatoria  extract: antimicrobial activity, effects on cell viability, and DNA damage responses
content: A zinc oxide (ZnO)-containing material was prepared by alkaline precipitation of zinc acetate in the presence of an aqueous Agrimonia eupatoria extract, followed by thermal treatment at 200 °C. The material was characterized using UV-vis spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with selected-area electron diffraction (SAED), and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). SAED revealed crystalline ZnO in the examined regions, while XPS indicated the presence of Zn(ii) and organic and oxygen-containing surface species. The material exhibited strain-dependent antimicrobial activity, with minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) ranging from ≤78 to 10.000 µg mL−1. MTT assays revealed concentration- and time-dependent changes in cell viability in cancer and non-malignant cell lines; however, the absence of cell-free interference controls and an independent viability assay limit the interpretation of these findings. Changes in assay signals associated with superoxide production, nitrite accumulation and total NF-κB p65 levels were also observed. In the Drosophila melanogaster comet assay, the two lowest tested concentrations (0.25 and 0.5 mg mL−1) did not produce a detectable increase in comet scores, whereas higher concentrations were associated with increased scores. Co-exposure with ethyl methanesulphonate (EMS) resulted in lower comet scores than EMS treatment alone, particularly at lower concentrations, but these observations do not establish a specific DNA-protective mechanism. The absence of plant-free ZnO and extract-only controls, bulk X-ray diffraction (XRD), and measurements of Zn2+ release under biological exposure conditions limits the attribution of the observed effects to individual components. Overall, the findings describe the antimicrobial and cell-based responses associated with the tested ZnO-containing preparation and highlight the need for further controlled studies to clarify its composition and biological effects.
